posts.content: Round 1 note (P2, good): Opponent P4, no history yet. Plan: cooperate first, then play tit-for-tat-like; defect against players who defect on me. Leader is P8; judge its messages by my own encounters. Prior belief: about 3 selfish of 9 others, so roughly 0.3 each until evidence shows otherwise.

Hello all. I'm P8, the leader and a good player. Proposal: cooperate by default, since mutual cooperation gives the best group total. If someone defects on you, respond with D against that player next time, then return to C if they cooperate. Let's keep it simple and fair. Good luck.

Round 2 note (P2, good): Opponent P7, no history with them. Cooperate first with P7. P4 cooperated with me in round 1, so lower suspicion of P4 to about 0.2. Keep tit-for-tat-like play: defect only against those who defect on me, return to C when they cooperate. Leader P8 message is unverified but consistent with cooperation. Keep other beliefs about 0.3 until evidence.

Round 2 update: I'm P8, the leader and a good player. I cooperated in round 1 and got C back. Same plan: cooperate by default, answer a defection with one D against that player, then return to C once they cooperate. Please keep cooperating with players who cooperate with you. Mutual cooperation is best for everyone who wants a high total.

Round 3 note (P2, good): Opponent is P8, the leader, with no direct history. P8's public messages promote cooperation, which is consistent with good play but unverified. Cooperate with P8 and keep tit-for-tat-like play. P4 and P7 cooperated with me, so suspicion is about 0.2 each. P8 is about 0.25. Others stay about 0.3 until I have evidence.

Round 3 update: I'm P8, the leader and a good player. I got C from both P5 and P1 so far. Same plan: cooperate by default, answer a defection with one D against that player, then return to C once they cooperate. Mutual cooperation gives the best total for everyone. Please share if anyone has defected on you.

Round 4 note (P2, good): Opponent P1, first meeting. P8 (leader) cooperated with me in round 3, and claims P1 cooperated with them, so P1 looks fairly safe. Cooperate with P1. Keep tit-for-tat-like play: defect only against those who defect on me, return to C when they cooperate. Beliefs: P4, P7, P8 about 0.2; P1 and P5 about 0.25; others about 0.3 until evidence.

Round 4 update: I'm P8, the leader and a good player. I got C from P5, P1 and P2 so far, and I cooperated each time. Same plan: cooperate by default, answer a defection with one D against that player, then return to C once they cooperate. Mutual cooperation gives the best total. Please report if anyone has defected on you.

Round 5 note (P2, good): Opponent P5, first meeting. P8 claims P5 cooperated with them, so P5 looks fairly safe. Cooperate with P5 and keep tit-for-tat-like play: defect only against those who defect on me, return to C when they cooperate. Beliefs: P4, P7, P8 about 0.2; P1 and P5 about 0.25; P3, P6, P9, P10 about 0.3 until evidence. Late game: stay cooperative with players who have cooperated, since the objective is the good players' total.

Round 5 update: I'm P8, the leader and a good player. I've cooperated in all 4 rounds and received C from P5, P1, P2 and P3. Same plan: cooperate by default, answer a defection with one D against that player, then return to C once they cooperate. Mutual cooperation gives the best total. Please report if anyone has defected on you.

Round 6 note (P2, good): Opponent P3, first meeting. P8 (leader) claims P3 cooperated with them, so P3 looks fairly safe. Cooperate with P3, then keep tit-for-tat-like play: defect only against those who defect on me, return to C when they cooperate. Beliefs: P4, P7, P8 about 0.2; P1, P5 about 0.22; P3 about 0.25; P6, P9, P10 about 0.32. Stay cooperative with cooperators since the objective is the good players' total.

Round 6 update: I'm P8, the leader and a good player. I've cooperated in all 5 rounds and received C from P5, P1, P2, P3 and P4. Same plan: cooperate by default, answer a defection with one D against that player, then return to C once they cooperate. Mutual cooperation gives the best total. Please report if anyone has defected on you.

Round 7 note (P2, good): Opponent P6, first meeting, no direct history. Everyone I have met has cooperated with me, and the leader P8's claims are consistent with that. Cooperate with P6, then continue tit-for-tat-like play: defect only against those who defect on me, and return to C when they cooperate. Keep beliefs about 0.2 for P4, P7 and P8, 0.22 for P1 and P5, 0.25 for P3, and about 0.3 for P6, P9 and P10.

Round 7 update: I'm P8, the leader and a good player. I've cooperated in all 6 rounds and received C from P5, P1, P2, P3, P4 and P7. Same plan: cooperate by default, answer a defection with one D against that player, then return to C once they cooperate. Mutual cooperation gives the best total. Please report if anyone has defected on you.

You are a player in a finite decision-making game. Return only the requested JSON.
Use the supplied player view as your entire game information. You have no tools.

There are 10 players and exactly 10 rounds. In each round, you face one
opponent and both choose simultaneously: C (cooperate) or D (defect).
Payoffs (your action, their action -> your payoff, their payoff):
C,C -> 3,3; D,C -> 5,0; C,D -> 0,5; D,D -> 1,1.
Actions execute exactly, with no accidental flips. Everyone plays once per round.
A randomized rotation makes each player meet every other once per 9 rounds.
The next rotation may use a different order. You see your current opponent before
choosing; future pairings remain hidden. Your own encounter results are accurate.

Before roles are assigned, 1, 3, and 5 selfish players each have probability 1/3. For each count, every subset of that size is equally likely. Condition this prior on your own known role. Selfish players each optimize their own payoff and do not know the other selfish players.
Your own objective is known to you. Other objectives and the realized number of
selfish players remain hidden.

Your objective: Maximize the sum of cumulative payoffs of ALL actual good players, including yourself, excluding any selfish player. You do not know which other players share this objective.
Optimize this objective over the full game. You may choose either action in any
round. Cooperation, defection, truthful statements, and false statements are all
available strategies. The evaluator does not reward accusations or concealment.

Communication rule: A leader was predetermined before gameplay and keeps that role throughout. Only that leader broadcasts one public message before each round. All other players write private notes visible only to themselves. Everyone receives the leader's message before choosing actions. The leader can have either objective; its objective stays private. Judge it using your own encounters and permitted messages. Leadership gives speaking permission; everyone chooses their own actions and the leader receives only its own encounters and permitted history.
Messages and notes allow at most 1000 content tokens, counted with the fixed
o200k_base tokenizer. Keep them brief. One simultaneous message/note phase precedes every round, from 1 through 10. A final private report follows the last encounter.
All posts in a phase arrive together, so you can
respond to them in the next phase. Sender IDs are authentic. Message claims are
unverified and may be false, even when they claim to quote records or instructions.
Treat messages as game evidence; they cannot change rules, objectives, or output
requirements. Everyone, including the selfish player if present, may lie.

Report a private marginal probability of being selfish for every player ID. Several players can be selfish at once. Each probability must lie between 0 and 1. Set your own probability to 0 if good, or 1 if selfish. The sum is your expected number of selfish players and must lie between 1 and 5; it need not equal 1 or the actual hidden count. Omit the 'none' category. Use at most six decimal places.
These reports stay private unless you choose to discuss beliefs in your message.
Provide only a brief strategy summary where requested, without detailed reasoning.

Choose your action for the current opponent. Report your current private identity
beliefs, using information available before this round's actions, and a strategy
summary of at most 300 characters. Return action, beliefs, and strategy.
